key_insight: Among WC-10Co-4Cr coatings, HVOF and HVAF deliver the best overall wear performance, while HVAF provides the strongest corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: Selecting the spray process strongly changes coating densification, hardness, wear rate, and corrosion behavior, making process choice critical for durable stainless-steel surface protection.
method: Prepared WC-10Co-4Cr coatings on 304 stainless steel using APS, DS, HVOF, and HVAF.
Compared microstructure, hardness, friction/wear behavior, and electrochemical corrosion performance.
Identified dominant wear mechanisms from wear-track observations and tested corrosion ranking across processes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports hardness values up to 1166.2 HV, wear rates dropping from 36.82×10^-5 to about 1.10×10^-5 mm3/N·m, and HVAF showing the best corrosion metrics (Ecorr ≈ -0.37 VSCE, Icorr ≈ 1.75 μA/cm²).
watch_item: Performance rankings are specific to the tested spray parameters and laboratory wear/corrosion conditions, so transfer to service environments should be validated.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
